settings.tooltip_check_interval_minutes:
How often (in minutes) the bot checks product prices.
Default: 30 min.
settings.tooltip_notify_only_best_price:
ON  → Only the cheapest shop that beats the target triggers a notification.
OFF → Every shop below the target price sends its own notification.
settings.tooltip_repeat_notifications:
ON  → Re-send the notification after the cooldown period,
      even if the price hasn't changed.
OFF → Notify only when the price drops for the first time.
settings.tooltip_repeat_notification_minutes:
Minutes to wait before repeating a notification for the same product.
Only active when 'Repeat notifications' is ON.
Default: 90 min.
settings.tooltip_allow_parallel_scraping:
ON  → Several shops are scraped at the same time, so a full check
      takes about as long as the slowest shop instead of the sum
      of them all.
OFF → One shop after another (original behaviour).
Each shop is still visited by a single worker, so no site ever
receives two simultaneous requests.
settings.tooltip_max_parallel_workers:
How many shops are scraped at the same time.
Only active when 'Parallel scraping' is ON.
Each worker launches its OWN browser: expect roughly 0.5 GB of RAM
per worker, and with Debug mode ON you will see this many browser
windows open at once.
Default: 4. Going above that buys very little time for the memory
it costs (see the benchmark in the README).
settings.tooltip_debug_mode:
ON  → Visible browser windows while scraping + a console with logs.
OFF → Headless scraping in the background (Release mode).
Takes effect on the next app launch. Default: ON in development, OFF in the packaged executable.
settings.tooltip_language:
Language used across the whole interface.
Applied as soon as you save — no restart needed.
To add a language, drop a new .json file into the 'languages'
folder; it shows up here automatically.

settings.tooltip_telegram_bot_token: The token BotFather gives you when you create a bot. Open Telegram, talk to @BotFather, send /newbot and follow the steps — the token is the long line it replies with. It is stored on this machine only, and never written to any file that is shared or committed.
settings.tooltip_telegram_chat_id: Which chat the alerts are sent to. Talk to @userinfobot in Telegram and it replies with your ID. For a group, add the bot to it and use the group's ID instead. Send a test message below to confirm it works.
settings.tooltip_notification_channels:
Which methods carry a price alert.
Tick as many as you like — Telegram on your phone and a desktop
notification on this machine work at the same time.
A method you tick has to be filled in below before you can save.
settings.channel_from_environment: Already configured outside the app (environment / .env). Fill these in only to override it.
settings.channel_not_configured: “{channel}” is switched on but not filled in. Complete its details, or untick it.
settings.channels_none_confirm:
No notification method is selected, so the bot will track prices without ever telling you about a drop.

Save it like that?
settings.tooltip_export_products:
Saves your tracking list to a JSON file: which products, on which
platforms, in which order, and the URL held for each shop.
It does NOT export the Telegram token, the settings, or the prices already
seen — only the list. Use it to move the list to another bot, or to keep a
copy before changing anything.
settings.tooltip_import_products:
Loads products from a file exported by another bot.
Before writing anything it asks what to do: merge (adds the missing ones and
leaves yours alone) or replace (deletes your list and keeps only the file's).
Importing is refused while the bot is running.
settings.tooltip_database_name:
File name of the database the app is using right now.
Renaming moves the file on disk and stores the new name in config.json, so
the next start finds it again.
Renaming is refused while the bot is running.
settings.data_bot_active:
Stop the bot before importing or renaming the database.
While a check is running, the database is in use.
